answer: Reputation-decay admission gate. Each new identity starts at a below-threshold trust score, so its first outputs route through a paid review queue whose fee exceeds the expected value of one successful spam payout. A clone therefore cannot reach the profitable tier before its accumulated fees cross the pearl of positive return. Scores decay on a fixed half-life, forcing every identity to keep paying to stay useful. This spiral of recurring cost means mass registration drives the operator's per-clone margin toward its nadir, so each additional identity is strictly negative-EV.
